newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REDONDO'S RETURN COULD KICK-START REAL'S TITLE CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REDONDO'S RETURN COULD KICK-START REAL'S TITLE CHALLENGE.

text.p: Real Madrid fans are hoping that the long-awaited return of midfield star Fernando Redondo this weekend will give their team the spark it's been lacking so far in the Spanish championship.
The Argentine international will make his comeback after missing five months through injury in Sunday's game at third- placed Oviedo.
Real lie fifth, with eight points from four matches, but are yet to display the kind of sparkle that was expected from their multi-billion peseta summer spending spree.
Redondo may do something to restore the panache to a side that has struggled since taking the 1995 championship.
But Redondo's skill has been matched by his tendency to pick up knocks, forcing the Real Madrid medical staff to put him through a series of special strengthening exercises.
His legs have grown 5 centimetres (2 inches) in diameter and his knees 3.5 centimetres (1.4 inches) as a result.
Redondo will support club captain Manolo Sanchis on the left, while teenager Raul Gonzalez will join Dutchman Clarence Seedorf on the right side of midfield.
Oviedo, unfancied before the start of the championship, are just one point behind leaders Real Betis and second placed Barcelona, and could even go top if they win.
Oviedo made Barcelona struggle before going down 4-2 in the first game of the season, but have subsequently won three consecutive games.
"One Real Madrid player cost all of our year's budget," remarked Oviedo coach Juan Manuel Lillo.
Spain's most expensive squad, Barcelona, travel to Zaragoza for a fixture that has produced goal avalanches for both sides in recent seasons.
But Bobby Robson's side are unlikely to maintain the record as striker Ronaldo is injured and doubtful for the game.
Barcelona have relied heavily on the Brazilian, and missed him in Thursday's goalless draw in the Cup Winners' Cup at LArnaca in Cyprus.
Table-toppers Real Betis face fourth-placed Deportivo Coruna on Saturday after a week in which the rival managers have gone to great lengths to praise each others' teams.

"Deportivo has got players with mangificent creativity in the midfield," said Betis' Serra Ferrer, while his opposite number at Deportivo, Welshman John Toshack said he believes Betis are good enough to win the league.
Betis may be without four first-choice players through injury, amongst them Nigerian international Finidi George Finidi, who has made his mark in Spain since signing from Ajax of Amsterdam.
Spain's UEFA Cup representatives all face straightforward games after overcoming their opponents in midweek.

Valencia travel to Compostela after knocking out holders Bayern Munich, Tenerife should have little problems against Sporting Gijon, while Espanyol are at home to Extremadura, a side that is yet to win a point in the first division.
Reigning champions Atletico Madrid face another newly promoted side, Hercules, on Monday.

Atletico will be without striker Kiko Narvaez, who was injured in the midweek Champions' League win in Poland, but coach Radomir Antic hopes to have midfielders Jose Luis Caminero and Juan Vizcaino fit to play.

The venue for Atletico's game against Sevilla next Thursday is in doubt after football authorities ordered Sevilla's Sanchez Pizjuan stadium to be closed after the referee in Monday's Sevilla-Compostela game was hit by a coin thrown from the stands.
Fixtures:
Saturday: Betis v La Coruna

Sunday: Compostela v Valencia; Espanyol v Extremadura; Logrones v Sevilla; Sociedad v Valladolid; Santander v Athletic Bilbao; Oviedo v Real Madrid; Tenerife v Sporting Gijon; Vallecano v Celta Vigo; Zaragoza v Barcelona
Monday: Atletico Madrid v Hercules
